CITY COUNCIL
MINUTES
CITY OF BALDWIN PARK
CITY COUNCIL
WEDNESDAY, AUGUST 05, 2009
7:00 p.m. COUNCIL CHAMBERS
14403 E. Pacific Avenue
Baldwin Park
Manuel Lozano, Mayor
Marlen Garcia, Mayor Pro Tem Monica Garcia, Ricardo Pacheco, Susan Rubio, Council Members
Maria Contreras, City Treasurer Alejandra Avila, City Clerk
The CITY COUNCIL of the City of Baldwin Park met in REGULAR SESSION at the above time and place.
CALL TO ORDER
INVOCATION
Led by Council member Pacheco
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE
ROLL CALL
Present: Council member Bejarano, Council member Marlen Garcia, Council member Pacheco, Mayor Pro Tem Monica Garcia, Mayor Lozano.
Absent: None.
Also Present: Chief Executive Officer Vijay Singhal, City Attorney Joseph W. Pannone, Director of Recreation & Community Services Manuel Carrillo Jr., Community Development Manager Marc Castagnola, Director of Public Works William Galvez, Director of Finance Lorena Quijano, City Treasurer Contreras, City Clerk Rubio, Deputy City Clerk Nieto.
ANNOUNCEMENTS
NONE
PROCLAMATIONS, COMMENDATIONS & PRESENTATIONS
Administration of Oath of Office and Certificates of Appointment for newly appointed and re-appointed Housing and Recreation & Community Services commissioners
Mayor Lozano administered the oaths of office to the newly appointed commissioners
Recognition of outgoing Recreation & Community Services student Commissioners Michael Arrelanes and Andrew Ruvalcaba
Certificate of Appreciation was presented to Andrew Ruvalcaba
PUBLIC COMMUNICATIONS
Thomas Cary , resident spoke about issues related to the city, financial institutions, actions of the state/Governor, transparency in government
Ana Saldana , LA County Animal Control Officer spoke about the officers being required to wear boots and that the County did not provide these to them. She requested the Council's support on the matter
Jorge Pivaral , Housing Commissioner thanked the Council for their support and offered to be of service to the community
Ken Woods , resident / business owner expressed his support of a downtown revitalization, but not the vision of the City Council. Felt that the project would not be for existing residents of the City
Rafael Gonzalez , Baldwin Park Librarian thanked Council member Marlen Garcia for inviting the Urban Book-Mobile to the Concerts in the Park; also thanked staff members Armando Nava and Rudolph Galindo for their assistance
Alfonso Contreras , resident expressed greetings from the dignitaries at Taxco, Guerrero, Baldwin Park’s Sister City and shared copies of newspaper articles published in Taxco during the Sister City’s visit
John Rios , resident thanked staff for cleaning up certain portions of the City but reported other areas that are in need of attention
Fidel Vargas, resident congratulated Recreation & Community Services staff on the new format of the the Baldwin Park NOW. He expressed concern about the lack of a pedestrian sidewalk near Bank of the West
Greg Tuttle , business owner spoke about the proposed Exclusive Negotiation Agreement with the Olson Company; commented about the Acevedo Group and Bisno Development and the contractor incentive program
Charlie Contreras, HLC Electric expressed his opposition to the staff recommendation to work with Watry for the design of a transit / parking structure
Cecelia Bernal , resident thanked the Council for their confidence by re-appointing her to the Commission and expressed her pride in the city
Public Communications were closed at 7:38 p.m.
Mayor Lozano expressed his support of the Animal Control Officers and stated that a letter of support would be sent. Mayor Lozano had been briefed on the matter by Mayor Pro Tem Monica Garcia
CONSENT CALENDAR
Motion: Approve CONSENT CALENDAR with the exception of Item #10
Moved by Mayor Lozano, seconded by Council member Marlen Garcia.
1. WARRANTS AND DEMANDS
Staff Report
City Council received and filed.
2. PROPOSED RECOGNITIONS BY THE MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL FOR THE PERIOD OF AUGUST 5, 2009 THROUGH AUGUST 18, 2009
Staff Report
City Council approved the preparation and presentation of the plaques and certificates as outlined in the staff report.
3. MINUTES
Staff Report
City Council approved the minutes of the regular meeting of July 1, 2009 and the special and regular meetings of July 15, 2009.
4. CITY TREASURER’S REPORT - JUNE 2009
Staff Report
City Council received and filed.
5. REQUEST TO HIRE A TECHNICAL FIRM TO ASSIST THE CITY WITH REVIEW OF THE DRAFT ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT REPORT BY THE CITY OF IRWINDALE FOR THE MATERIALS RECOVERY FACILITY AND TRANSFER STATION (MRF/TS)LOCATED AT THE INTERSECTION OF LIVE OAK AVENUE AND ARROW HWY
Staff Report
City Council 1) authorized the Chief Executive Officer to enter into a Consultant Services Agreement with ESA for a not to exceed amount of $31,540 to provide the City with technical expertise in reviewing the City of Irwindale's DEIR for the MRF/TS located at the intersection of Arrow Highway and Live Oak Avenue and 2) authorized a transfer of funds from 100.00.299.53999.00000.2 in the amount of $31,450 into account 100.40.440.51100.00000.2
6. RENEWAL OF AGREEMENT WITH ALL CITY MANAGEMENT SERVICES FOR PROVIDING SCHOOL CROSSING GUARD SERVICES FOR FISCAL YEAR 2009/2010
Staff Report
City Council 1) approved the FY 09/10 contract with All City Management Services for crossing guard services and 2) authorized the Mayor to execute the agreement to continue services with All City Management Services.
7. RESOLUTION NO. 2009-035 AUTHORIZING THE EXECUTION OF A MASTER AGREEMENT AND PROGRAM SUPPLEMENTS FOR FEDERALLY FUNDED PROJECTS
Staff Report
City Council adopted Resolution No. 2009-035 entitled, "A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF BALDWIN PARK, CALIFORNIA, AUTHORIZING THE EXECUTION OF A MASTER AGREEMENT AND PROGRAM SUPPLEMENTS FOR FEDERALLY FUNDED PROJECTS."
8. APPROVAL TO ADOPT AND ADHERE TO THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY GREEN RESOLUTION, RESOLUTION NO. 2009-032, CREATION OF AND ACCESSIBILITY TO REGION-WIDE PASSIVE / ACTIVE GREEN SPACE AND CONNECTORS
Staff Report
City Council adopted Resolution No. 2009-032 entitled, "A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF BALDWIN PARK AUTHORIZING THE ADOPTION AND ADHERENCE TO THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY GREEN RESOLUTION, CREATION FO AND ACCESSIBILITY TO REGION-WIDE PASSIVE / ACTIVE GREEN SPACE & CONNECTORS" and authorized the Mayor to execute any other associated documents related to this initiative.
9. NOTICE OF COMPLETION AND PROJECT ACCEPTANCE OF FIRE DAMAGE REPAIRS TO THE ESTHER SNYDER COMMUNITY CENTER
Staff Report
City Council 1) accepted the construction improvements by Simgel Company, Inc.; 2) considered the project complete and authorize the recordation of a Notice of Completion; and 3) authorized the payment of retention funds to Simgel Company Inc. upon expiration of the 35-day lien period.
The following item was pulled by Council member Pacheco for spearate discussion:
10. AUTHORIZE STAFF TO ENGAGE WATRY DESIGN, INC. FOR ARCHITECTURAL AND ENGINEERING SERVICES FOR THE TRANSIT CENTER PARKING STRUCTURE AND AUTHORIZE THE CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER TO FINALIZE A CONSULTANT SERVICES AGREEMENT IN AN AMOUNT NOT TO EXCEED $595,900
Staff Report
Council member Pacheco commented about the history of this project and was looking forward to this being approved
Motion: Approve hiring Watry Design, Inc. for Architecture and Engineering Services for the Transit Center Parking Structure and authorize the Chief Executive Officer and City Attorney to finalize a Consultant Services Agreement with Watry Design, Inc for Design and Construction Support for an amount not to exceed $595,900.
Moved by Council member Pacheco, seconded by Council member Bejarano.
SET MATTERS - PUBLIC HEARINGS
11. PUBLIC HEARING TO ADOPT A RESOLUTION AND THE CITY’S 2009 CONGESTION MANAGEMENT PROGRAM LOCAL IMPLEMENTATION REPORT
Staff Report
City Planner Harbin presented the report. Mayor Lozano opened the public hearing for those wishing to speak in favor or opposition. Seeing no interest the public hearing was closed
Motion: Adopt Resolution No. 2009-031 entitled, "A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF BALDWIN PARK FINDING THE CITY TO BE IN CONFORMANCE WITH THE CONGESTION MANAGEMENT PROGRAM (CMP) AND ADOPTING THE CMP LOCAL DEVELOPMENT REPORT IN ACCORDANCE WITH CALIFORNIA GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 65089."
Moved by Mayor Lozano, seconded by Council member Pacheco.
12. PUBLIC HEARING FOR PROPOSED INSTALLATION OF MULTI-WAY STOP SIGN CONTROLS AT FOUR RESIDENTIAL INTERSECTIONS
Staff Report
Public Works Director Galvez presented the report. Mayor Lozano opened the public hearing for those wishing to speak in favor or opposition.
FAVOR:
Thomas Cary
Jorge Pivaral
OPPOSITION:
NONE
Seeing no further interest, the public hearing was closed.
Council member Pacheco spoke about the importance of the installation of these stop signs, requested that areas with high traffic and near schools be prioritized; Mayor Pro Tem Monica Garcia congratulated and thanked staff for prioritizing this project. She asked that the residents in the immediate areas be contacted so that they can take credit for this joint accomplishment; Council member Bejarano thanked staff, noting that constitutents have brought this problem to his attention. Requested that staff be vigilant about traffic situations in the city, noting that the 4-way stop at Merced and Big Dalton may need to be patrolled because drivers had been running the sign. Council member Marlen Garcia expressed her concern regarding the traffic in the city, noting that it was perfect timing for the installation of these traffic calming measures because the traffic in the city would only get worse
Motion: Authorize staff to proceed with the installation of stop sign controls at the proposed four locations.
Moved by Mayor Lozano, seconded by Council member Bejarano.
CITY COUNCIL/ CITY CLERK / CITY TREASURER / STAFF REQUESTS & COMMUNICATIONS
Mayor Pro Tem Monica Garcia requested that a resolution of support be brought forward at the next City Council meeting in support of the Animal Control Officers request for work boots
ADJOURNMENT
There being no other matters for discussion the meeting was adjourned at 8:56 p.m.
Approved as presented by the Council at their meeting held September 2, 2009.
Laura M. Nieto, CMC
Deputy City Clerk
